literal: The great wealth obtained by one who lacks good character is like good milk curdled because of the impurity of the vessel.
translation: The great wealth acquired by a person devoid of good character is like wholesome milk that turns sour and spoils because of the impurity of the vessel containing it.
modern: நற்பண்பு இல்லாதவன் பெற்ற பெரிய செல்வமானது, பாத்திரத்தின் அழுக்கால் நல்ல பால் கெட்டுப் போவதைப் போன்றதாகும்.
explanation: This couplet uses a vivid analogy to show how wealth is wasted on someone without good character. Just as fresh, wholesome milk (நன்பால்) becomes sour and useless when poured into an unclean or defective vessel (கலம்), great wealth (பெருஞ்செல்வம்) loses its value and becomes ruined when possessed by a person who lacks courtesy and virtue (பண்பிலான்). The focus is on the container: the wealth itself may be good, but the character of the owner determines whether it remains beneficial or goes to waste. Thus, cultivating good character is essential before acquiring or holding great resources.
